headlines.title: Bicyclist killed in hit-and-run collision in San Jose
headlines.description: A bicyclist was killed in a hit-and-run collision in San Jose early Friday morning, according to police. The collision happened around 6:15 a.m. in the area of East Capitol Expressway and Ocala Avenue. The bicyclist died from their injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene, police said. The collision is under investigation. East Capitol Expressway at Ocala Avenue is blocked in all directions and is expected to remain closed while officers investigate. Drivers are being asked to avoid the area and use alternate routes. Additional information was not immediately available. This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

headlines.title: 49ers star edge rusher Nick Bosa out ‘few weeks' after pulling calf, per report
headlines.description: The 49ers again will be without star edge rusher Nick Bosa for an extended period. Bosa pulled his calf during practice this week and will miss “a few weeks,” ESPN’s Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported Friday, citing sources. Bosa played on 63 percent of the 49ers’ defensive snaps during the first two games of the season, but he popped up on the injury report Thursday. NBC Sports Bay Area’s Jennifer Lee Chan hinted at a potentially serious Bosa injury late Thursday. “Nick Bosa was supposed to talk to us on Wednesday,” Chan said during a YouTube live stream. “That was his media day. He did not talk to us on Wednesday and then he did not talk to us today, Thursday. We waited around for him. And … knee and calf. It’s not good. I just don’t think … It doesn’t feel good. Like, my spidey senses are saying that this is a serious injury for Nick Bosa, and if he’s not out for the season, he’s out for multiple weeks.” At least for the moment, it appears Bosa and the 49ers dodged the “out for the season” bullet. Bosa missed most of the 2025 NFL season after tearing his ACL early in the year. Bosa’s injury is the latest blow to the 49ers’ defensive line, with Alfred Collins already out for the season, and Sam Okuayinonu and CJ West on injured reserve. James Thompson Jr. is expected to miss time with an ankle injury and rookie Romello Height underwent surgery for a fractured hand, putting his status for Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals in doubt. The 49ers had big expectations for Bosa this season and now he will be sidelined for several weeks. headlines.title: 3 hospitalized, dozens displaced after apartment fire in Oakland
headlines.description: Dozens of people were displaced and three were hospitalized after an early morning fire at an apartment complex in Oakland on Friday. The three-alarm fire broke out on Bancroft Avenue near 51st Avenue and International Boulevard just before 1 a.m. Fire crews rescued several people from the second floor of the building. Three people were taken to a nearby hospital. The fire has since been extinguished. The cause of the fire was not immediately known.

headlines.title: Tom Holland, Oakland native Zendaya spotted in Marin County
headlines.description: Fresh off a busy summer, actors Tom Holland and Oakland native Zendaya have been spotted spending time in the North Bay. Video posted on TikTok showed the pair walking at The Village at Corte Madera earlier this week. On Thursday, Holland also snapped a selfie with servers at Mixt, a salad chain in Mill Valley. The newlyweds co-starred in two major blockbusters this summer, “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” Their appearances come as social media has been filled with rumors that the couple bought a home in Tiburon.

headlines.title: Family, friends continue search 6 months after Amy Hillyard disappeared
headlines.description: The husband of missing coffee shop owner Amy Hillyard issued an appeal to keep her story visible, on the six-month anniversary of her disappearance in March. Chris Hillyard said in a video that investigators and supporters continue to search for answers, and are focusing the search on specific areas, using drones to hunt for clues in areas where Amy liked to hike and walk. “The private investigator who’s worked on missing persons cases across the country called Amy’s disappearance one of the most perplexing cases he’s ever worked on,” Chris Hillyard said in the video. The owner of Farley’s coffee shops in Oakland and San Francisco, 52-year-old Amy Hillyard was last seen on March 25, sometime after 2 p.m. near the 500 block of Radnor Road in Oakland. Amy is described as white, 5 feet 4 inches tall, weighing about 120 pounds, with blonde hair and hazel eyes. She was wearing a white short-sleeved shirt, light-colored jeans, and white sneakers with black stripes. She is considered at risk due to a medical condition. It’s been six months and her friends and family haven’t given up on the search. “Still we all keep trying and every day we wake up with a glimmer of hope that today will the day that brings some piece of information that offers an answer to Amy’s whereabouts,” Chris Hillyard said. A $25,000 reward for information on Hillyard’s disappearance is still in effect. The video can be found at https://www.youtube.com/shorts/ajqClXNBv48 and at Bringamyhome.com, a site created by Amy’s friends and family where supporters can stay up to date on the status of current efforts to find Hillyard. The site also has various ways that people can help in the search.

A multi-day air show, parade of ships and ship tours highlight the weeklong festivities. “San Francisco Fleet Week is an annual public event that honors the contributions of the men and women of the United States Armed Forces while advancing cooperation and knowledge among civilian- and military-based Humanitarian Assistance personnel,” a statement on the event’s website reads. headlines.title: Bay Area gas prices jump about 70 cents in a month
headlines.description: Drivers across the Bay Area are paying significantly more at the pump than they were a month ago, according to new numbers from AAA. The average price for a gallon of gas in California jumped another 15 cents over the past week to $6.23. Prices are even higher in parts of the Bay Area. In Oakland, the average price is $6.35 a gallon, up from $5.61 a month ago. San Francisco’s average climbed to $6.47 from $5.74, while San Jose’s rose to $6.30 from $5.57. That’s an increase of around 70 cents a gallon in just one month. Some individual stations are charging even more. A Chevron station in Dublin was charging $6.79 a gallon Friday morning, while a Shell station in San Francisco was charging $7.29. Nationwide, the average price for a gallon of gas is $4.48, the highest the national average has ever been for this time of year. NBC Bay Area’s Bob Redell has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: Bay Area voter guide: What to know about the November 2026 election
headlines.description: What to Know — Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026 California will choose a new governor to replace Gavin Newsom, who terms out after this year. The choices are Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton. Voters will decide 14 state propositions. Regional sales tax Measure RTM, the Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, aims to increase funds for public transit. California’s Congressional District 11 race features Scott Wiener and Connie Chan competing to succeed Nancy Pelosi. Aisha Wahab and Melissa Hernandez will face off again after a special election in August where Wahab secured victory to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. All 80 California Assembly seats are up for reelection, as well as 20 Senate seats. California’s general election is Nov. 3, with statewide races and propositions as well as key local races and measures across the Bay Area. Here’s what you need to know to cast your ballot, including important dates and deadlines, how to register or check your status, where and when to vote, and what’s on the ballot. Key election dates The last day to register to vote for the Nov. 3 general election is Oct. 19. County election officials will start mailing ballots by Oct. 5. Ballot drop-off locations open on Oct. 6 Last day to register to vote for the general election is Oct. 19. First vote centers open for early in-person voting in all Voter’s Choice Act counties on Oct. 24. In person early voting locations in the state open on Oct. 31. Election Day, Nov. 3, is the last day to vote in-person or return a ballot by 8 p.m. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Vote-by-mail ballots must be postmarked no later than Nov. 3. If mailing on election day, get a hand-stamped postmark from a postal employee inside a post office. Visit the California Secretary of State’s website for a full list of key dates and deadlines. Check voter registration status Voters can check their registration at voterstatus.sos.ca.gov to confirm their mailing address and voting status. How to register to vote California residents can register to vote in elections at registertovote.ca.gov. Note Oct. 19 is the last day to register for the general election. Same day voter registration window will be open from Oct. 20 up to the Nov. 3 election day. Visit caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov for a list of early voting locations to complete same day registration. How to find your polling place Visit the California Secretary of State’s website, where you can input your address to find your polling location and see what is on your ballot. Voters can also visit their county elections office for more information. Scroll down to the Bay Area county election offices section of this guide for further contact information. What to bring to your polling place Voters usually are not required to show identification to a polling place worker before casting a ballot, according to the Secretary of State’s website. There are some instances when providing identification is required: Voting for the first time after registering to vote by mail and did not provide a driver license number California identification number or the last four digits of social security number are missing on registration form In these cases voters should plan to bring identification to a polling place or bring a copy of it with their vote-by-mail ballot. The Secretary of State says the following are acceptable forms of identification: Passport Driver license Official state identification card Student identification card Copy of recent utility bill Sample ballot booklet received from county elections office Any document received by a government agency How to track your mail-in ballot Voters can track their vote-by-mail ballot and confirm it has been received by using the state’s Where’s My Ballot? tool at california.ballottrax.net/voter/. Ballots mailed in may take a few days to appear on the website. Why is California choosing a new governor? Gov. Gavin Newsom terms out after this year and voters will choose between Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton, who both advanced to the general election after a wild primary. Becerra has served as former President Joe Biden’s top health official and oversaw the response to the coronavirus pandemic. He was also the California’s attorney general during President Donald Trump’s first term and has more than two decades of experience as a congressmember. Hilton was a conservative commentator with a show on Fox News for six years. He also worked as an adviser to former British prime minister David Cameron. What are the 14 California propositions voters will decide in the November election? Here’s a list of the California propositions on the November ballot and descriptions from the secretary of state: Proposition 1: Authorizes bonds for housing affordability programs Proposition 2: Increases state’s rainy day fund Proposition 3: Provides permanent funding for schools and healthcare by extending existing tax on high incomes Proposition 4: Repeals prohibition against public funding of election campaigns. Proposition 5: Changes recall election process for statewide officers. Proposition 37: Creates loan program for middle-income buyers of qualified new homes. Proposition 38: Authorizes bonds for immunology medical research. Proposition 39: Prohibits citizens from voting unless they present government-issued identification. Proposition 40: Imposes one-time tax on certain taxpayers. Proposition 41: Prohibits new state taxes that exclude revenues from state spending limit. Requires audits for new state special taxes. Proposition 42: Prohibits new state personal property taxes and certain retroactive state taxes. Proposition 43: Limits voters’ ability to raise revenues for local government services. Proposition 44: Requires community health clinics spend 90% of revenue on program services. Proposition 45: Modifies environmental review for certain projects. Regional measure to watch Measure RTM: The Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, is a regional sales tax aimed at increasing funds for public transit. It includes 5 Bay Area counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara. Races and measures to watch in Alameda County California Congressional District 14: California lawmaker Aisha Wahab and Bay Area Rapid Transit Director Melissa Hernandez will face off again to determine who will serve the next full two-year term. Wahab topped Hernandez in an August special election to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. Swalwell resigned from Congress earlier this year after sexual assault and misconduct allegations. District 14 includes the East Bay cities such as Fremont, Hayward and Livermore. Measure X in Berkeley: Would establish 10% limit on annual rent increases and other changes to the city’s rent ordinance. Measure Y in Berkeley: Parcel tax to pay for arts projects. Measure Z in Berkeley: Parcel tax to fund a public bank. Measure AA in Berkeley: Increase soda tax (not assigned) Measure EE in Oakland: Shift city to a strong mayor system. Measure FF in Oakland: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Alameda County and additional election information, visit the Alameda County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Contra Costa County In Contra Costa County, several county board of education seats are open. In Richmond, residents will vote on a new mayor while voters in San Pablo will weigh in on Measure S, which would limit rent increases. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Contra Costa County and additional election information, visit the Contra Costa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Napa County California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. Measure B in Napa County: Sales tax to fund wildfire prevention and open space preservation. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Napa County and additional election information, visit the Napa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Francisco San Francisco voters will weigh in on several open seats on the county board of supervisors and board of education. Proposition A: Give mayor more power to hire and fire department heads. Proposition B: Pave way for public bank. Proposition C: Increase the city’s annual contribution to an affordable housing trust fund. Proposition D: New barriers to placing measures on the ballot. Proposition E: Changes to city contracting. Proposition G: Reopen parts of the Great Highway to vehicle traffic on weekdays. Proposition H: Parcel tax to fund Muni. Proposition J: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax California Congressional District 11: Scott Wiener and Connie Chan compete to succeed Nancy Pelosi. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Francisco and additional election information, visit the San Francisco Department of Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Mateo County Measure E in Redwood City: Limit rent increases. Measure Q in Half Moon Bay: Referendum to block proposed farmworker housing. Measure U in San Mateo County: Create independent commission to draw supervisor districts. For a complete list of San Mateo County measures and races on the ballot, visit smacre.gov/elections. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Mateo County and additional election information, visit the San Mateo County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Santa Clara County In San Jose, incumbents Peter Ortiz and Bien Doan are up for re-election in Districts 5 and 7, respectively, and there’s an open seat in District 9. Races and measures to watch in Solano County Solano County Board of Supervisors, District 4: Mike Silva and John Carli face in a runoff in a district covering Vacaville and Dixon. Measure E in Solano County: New tax on data centers and battery storage facilities in the unincorporated county areas. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Solano County and additional election information, visit the Solano County Registrar of Voters website. Races and measures to watch in Sonoma County California Congressional District 1: Mike McGuire will face James Gallagher in a seat redistricted by Proposition 50. California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. State Assembly District 12: Eric Lucan and Jackie Elward compete in a battle between business and labor. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Sonoma County and additional election information, visit the Sonoma County Registrar of Voters website. headlines.title: Worried about being shortchanged at the gas pump? Here's what to look for
headlines.description: Have you ever wondered if a gas pump is actually delivering what you’re paying for? It’s a question many people across the country are asking as high prices persist. In the South Bay, the task of checking fuel pump accuracy falls on Santa Clara County’s Weights and Measures Division. “We’re out there every day making sure the customers can feel confident in the gas that they’re buying,” said Ryan Atwood with the Weights and Measures Division. When filling up, consumers should keep an eye out for a seal on the pump that indicates it passed inspection. A pump that pumps too much gas favors customers, but still gets a blue tag, meaning repairs should be made within 30 days. A red tag means the pump is not pouring enough gas and is immediately shut down. What the county doesn’t want to see is people testing the accuracy of a gas pump themselves. The county said that dangerous task should be left to the professionals. “I’m assuring them that if they see one of our seals at the pump, they can be assured that that pump is accurate,” Atwood said. oil and gas Sep 22 oil and gas Sep 17

headlines.title: How the 49ers play into this year's Santa Clara mayoral race
headlines.description: The San Francisco 49ers find themselves in the midst of the hotly contested race for mayor of Santa Clara, the city the team calls home. Santa Clara does not have a primary election for mayor, so all six candidates are on the ballot in November. The 49er influence on voters, whether positive or negative, matters significantly. Supporters of mayoral candidate and former city councilmember Kathy Watanabe gathered near Levi’s Stadium Thursday to cheer her call for an independent audit of how much the 49ers and Levi’s Stadium pay into the city’s general fund, especially from recent big events, such as the Super Bowl and World Cup matches. Their complaints echoed a civil grand jury report a couple years ago that recommended Santa Clara conduct its own economic impact analysis. “When a public asset generates private revenue and profits, the public deserves transparency,” Watanabe said. “This shouldn’t be about being pro-49ers or even anti-49ers. It should be about being pro-Santa Clara.” The 49ers emphatically counter that they are a good partner with Santa Clara and transparent in their financial payments to the city. The franchise offered a list of local businesses that they say benefit from the 49ers and Levi’s Stadium. The 49ers, citing public records, said stadium revenue has generated more than $30 million to Santa Clara’s general fund in the past two years and said “Ms. Watanabe is either misinformed or intentionally misleading the public.” David Kertes, another mayoral candidate, said audits are nice but not enough and blamed city leadership for any lack of transparency with the 49ers. In a statement, the city said, so far, it has received about 95% of the reimbursement it expected to get from the 49ers and confirmed the city made about $3 million from Super Bowl hotel tax revenue. All of the mayoral candidates will get a chance to address the issues at a debate this Sunday.

headlines.title: Man who allegedly confessed to killing 2 people in San Jose appears in court
headlines.description: A man accused of killing two people along a South Bay trail appeared in court on Thursday. Investigators say Marcelino Castro admitted to the murders along the Guadalupe Park Trail and led officers to the bodies of both victims. The investigation began Saturday, after police say Castro flagged down an officer. Police say he confessed to two killings and led officers to the bodies. The DA’s Office says it believes the first murder happened on Sept. 13, and the second a few days later. “Based on that timeline, we’re concerned, had another 24-48 hours passed, we may have had another murder,” Deputy District Attorney Michael Gadeberg said. In both cases the motive is still under investigation. As of now, Gadeberg says there’s no indication there are more victims, but they’re still investigating. “We’re certainly still investigating all possible leads and all avenues, I wouldn’t rule out the possibility that there’s another victim and we’re continuing to look into that,” he said. “It appears that this is someone who was a thrill killer, that sought these victims out, very vicious crimes and prosecutors can’t take this for granted that these are the only victims out there. I think law enforcement needs to keep an open mind about this case,” legal analyst Steven Clark said. Clark says even though investigators have a confession, building a case will still be essential. “Law enforcement cannot take anything for granted in this case, they not only need to use the confession but they need to tie him to these murders forensically, are there witnesses? Is his DNA at the crime scene?” he said. Castro is being held without bail and is expected back in court in December. While investigators haven’t commented on his criminal history, San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan released a statement, indicating the suspect has one. The mayor posted on social media that Castro should be held fully accountable, adding, “But how does someone rack up six felony convictions, face two more active felony cases, and keep cycling through the system as things get worse? How and why was he released in the first place? At some point, intervention has to mean more than processing the next case and sending someone back out.” The victims have not been identified.

headlines.title: Activists rally after incident involving day laborers at Concord Home Depot
headlines.description: Pro-immigration groups gathered outside Home Depot in Concord on Thursday to protest what they say was the detention of four day laborers. They believe federal agents were involved, but the two most likely agencies said they weren’t. The Concord Immigrants Protections Network said a witness gave one of its volunteers a video showing what appeared to be federal agents detaining four day laborers at a Home Depot parking lot. “He was able to speak to witnesses who told him that four day laborers were taken into these unmarked SUVs,” Tony Bravo with the Concord Immigrant Protections Network said. However, NBC Bay Area’s sister station Telemundo 48 contacted ICE and CBP, and the agencies said they weren’t the ones that made the arrests. Activists say what happened is causing some panic, regardless of which agency was involved. In a statement, Home Depot said in part, “We aren’t notified that immigration enforcement activities are going to happen, and we aren’t involved in the operations. We aren’t coordinating with ICE or Border Patrol. We cannot legally interfere with federal enforcement agencies.” Activists said they don’t have any information on who the detainees are.
